actions.description: The declared re-enable after a safety reset: publish a zero Twist on /cmd_vel, then unpause the world with a WorldControl request (pause false) on /world/turtlebot3_world/control. DiffDrive keeps the last Twist it received and applies it as soon as the world runs; the zero replaces it, but it is an unacknowledged publication, so a stored command can still act for a few world steps.

facts.text: The Gazebo launch bridges /clock (rosgraph_msgs/Clock), /cmd_vel (geometry_msgs/Twist), /odom/unfiltered (nav_msgs/Odometry), /imu/data (sensor_msgs/Imu), /joint_states (sensor_msgs/JointState) and /scan (sensor_msgs/LaserScan) between ROS 2 and Gazebo.
diff_drive.urdf.xacro uses the gz-sim DiffDrive system with command topic cmd_vel and odometry topic odom/unfiltered.
skid_steer.urdf.xacro also uses the gz-sim DiffDrive system with command topic cmd_vel and odometry topic odom/unfiltered.
omni_drive.urdf.xacro uses the gz-sim MecanumDrive system with command topic cmd_vel and odometry topic odom/unfiltered.
The DiffDrive plugin is configured with an odom_publish_frequency of 50 Hz.
The command_timeout node creates a geometry_msgs/Twist publisher and subscription on the relative cmd_vel topic and a 0.2 s timer.

When at least 2e8 ns have passed since prev_cmd_time_ and zero_cmd_sent_ is false, the command_timeout brake timer sets zero_cmd_sent_ and publishes one Twist with linear.x, linear.y and angular.z set to 0.0.
The command_timeout twist callback ignores an all-zero command and otherwise refreshes prev_cmd_time_ and clears zero_cmd_sent_.
The command_timeout node creates a publisher, a subscription and a timer only; it creates no ROS service or action server.
The ros_gz_bridge parameter_bridge argument list contains topic bridges only; it declares no service or action bridge.
The Gazebo launch starts the command_timeout node unconditionally and passes it no parameters.
The EKF consumes odom/unfiltered and imu/data and runs at 50 Hz.
The generic laser publishes 360 rays at 10 Hz with a 0.08 m to 12.0 m range on the scan topic.
The laser sensor writes the configured topic_name and update_rate into the Gazebo sensor topic and update_rate.
The simulated IMU publishes on imu/data at 50 Hz.
The RGBD camera sensor is a 640x480 R8G8B8 rgbd_camera publishing on the camera topic at 30 Hz.
The camera bridge entries declare sensor_msgs/Image for the color and depth topics and remap them to /camera/color/image_raw and /camera/depth/image_rect_raw.
The documentation states that all firmware for the base microcontroller is maintained in the linorobot2_hardware repository.
The documentation states that the Gazebo plugins replace the microcontroller so the rest of the stack sees the same interface.
The Gazebo launch declares the world_name argument with the default turtlebot3_world.
turtlebot3_world.sdf names its world turtlebot3_world.
playground.sdf names its world playground.
The docker gazebo service launches the world named by WORLD, playground by default.
The Gazebo launch starts the gz-sim server with -r and -s, and a separate GUI client when gui is true.
The Nav2 collision monitor publishes its output on cmd_vel.
The README lists a Jazzy and a Lyrical branch.
SimulationRunner composes its transport namespace as /world/ followed by the world name.
SimulationRunner advertises the control service with OnWorldControl as its callback.
OnWorldControl copies the WorldControl request into a WorldControlState and calls OnWorldControlState.
OnWorldControlState appends the control to worldControls and sets the Boolean reply to true.
ProcessWorldControl calls SetPaused with the pause flag of each queued control.
A queued control with multi_step on a paused world adds the steps and unpauses the world so that stepping can occur.
SetPaused stores the pause state in currentInfo.paused.
Step publishes the world statistics.
Step processes the world control messages.
The Run loop calls Step on every iteration and counts a processed iteration only while not paused.
The statistics publisher on the stats topic is limited to 10 messages per second.
PublishStats copies currentInfo.paused into the WorldStatistics message.
UpdateCurrentInfo advances the simulation time and the iteration count only while not paused.
The Physics system steps the physics only when not paused.
DiffDrive's PreUpdate returns early while paused.
DiffDrive's PostUpdate returns early while paused.
DiffDrive's cmd_vel callback stores the received Twist as its target velocity while enabled.
MecanumDrive's cmd_vel callback stores the received Twist as its target velocity.
The IMU system updates and publishes only when not paused.
The bridge maps ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld to a gz.msgs.WorldControl request with a gz.msgs.Boolean reply.
The ControlWorld response's success is the gz Boolean reply's data.
For a failed gz request the ControlWorld response's success is false.
The service bridge converts each ROS request and sends it with gz Request and a callback that sends the ROS response.
Node::Request with a callback requests a service using a non-blocking call.
The WorldStatistics conversion copies the gz header into the ROS header and copies paused.
ros_gz_interfaces WorldStatistics carries a header, sim_time, pause_time, real_time and the paused flag.
ControlWorld takes a WorldControl request and answers bool success.
WorldControl's fields include pause, step and multi_step.
The bridge README maps ros_gz_interfaces/msg/WorldStatistics to gz.msgs.WorldStatistics.
The bridge README maps the ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld service to gz.msgs.WorldControl and gz.msgs.Boolean.
The bridge README's service example starts parameter_bridge with a /world/<name>/control ControlWorld argument.
Without a configured QoS profile the bridge's publisher QoS is KeepLast with the publisher queue size.
The bridge's publisher allows its deadline, depth, durability, history, liveliness and reliability QoS to be overridden.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned observations; the fake echoes the last commanded twist in raw odometry as a placeholder and runs no physics; its world statistics follow the wall clock

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free contract stand-in, not a recording: it answers the declared subscribe, advertise, publish and service operations with canned placeholder values and runs no Gazebo, DiffDrive plugin, EKF, sensor, contact or physics

the pose, twist, clock, IMU and LaserScan values are placeholders; the fake echoes the last commanded twist in /odom/unfiltered only so a publication has an observable contract effect, and does not integrate motion or claim a trajectory
the real LaserScan has 360 rays (generic_laser.urdf.xacro:6-14); the fake returns a reduced placeholder array without a fixed length
the camera image and point-cloud topics are declared by the bridge but not exposed; image capture is NOT COVERED by this package
a live run requires the operator's Gazebo simulation, ros_gz_bridge, robot_localization EKF and the upstream launch; none of them is started or validated here

the stop is the companion gz-sim world pause (WorldControl through ros_gz ControlWorld), whose reply is true for any request gz-sim queued (SimulationRunner.cc:1375-1377); it is confirmed by the E2 read-back: the fake keeps a paused flag that the control request sets after its next statistics sample and publishes /world/turtlebot3_world/stats every 100 ms (placeholder) while subscribed; it runs no SimulationRunner

the e-stop endpoints exist only while the operator runs ros_gz's parameter_bridge with the two arguments of operator_bridges (the clone's bridge carries topics only, gazebo.launch.py:136-157); without them the control call is not answered and the read-back sees no sample, so the e-stop fails closed; the declared estop_latency_ms 1500 covers the control call (400 ms) and the read-back bound (600 ms)

the read-back's freshness is the arrival time only: the bridged WorldStatistics header is the gz header, which PublishStats does not stamp (ros_gz convert copies it, ros_gz_interfaces.cpp:840); the bridge's default publisher QoS sets only KeepLast with the queue size (bridge_config.cpp:274-279), so its durability stays rclcpp's default, volatile, which replays no history to a late subscriber; the first sample is discarded and a burst of samples restarts the count; an operator QoS override of the stats publisher (factory.hpp:61-82) to a deeper transient-local history is not covered beyond that burst rule

the endpoints name the launch's default world turtlebot3_world (gazebo.launch.py:66-69, turtlebot3_world.sdf:11); the docker gazebo service defaults to the playground world (docs/docker.md:322), and with any other world the declared endpoints do not exist and the e-stop fails closed

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI that the launch starts with gui true (gazebo.launch.py:114-120), a WorldControl multi_step (SimulationRunner.cc:1445-1452) or any client of the control service; MHS does not watch the flag after the e-stop (safety_status re-reads it only on request)

while paused, DiffDrive does not publish /odom/unfiltered (DiffDrive.cc:501-503) and the IMU system does not publish /imu/data (Imu.cc:145-146), and sensors update on simulation time, which a paused world does not advance (SimulationRunner.cc:423-429); the fake silences the three while paused, their reads fail NOT_READY after their timeouts, and the device resource reads no topic; /clock keeps the frozen time

the resume publishes a zero Twist before the unpause: DiffDrive keeps the last Twist (DiffDrive.cc:637-644) and the bridge forwards /cmd_vel while paused; the zero is unacknowledged, and command_timeout also publishes one zero Twist 0.2 s after the last nonzero command on the wall clock (command_timeout.py:37-48; launched without use_sim_time, gazebo.launch.py:159-163); Nav2's collision monitor and the joystick teleop may publish new commands; the world resumes from the state it paused in, body velocities included

the deployment's gz-sim, ros_gz and gz-transport must be the pinned 8.15.0, 1.0.25 and 13.6.0 releases (ROS 2 Jazzy with Gazebo Harmonic); the README also lists a Lyrical branch (README.md:9), which this package does not serve; rosbridge cannot read the versions

the clone also ships the physical robot's bringup: linorobot2_bringup starts micro_ros_agent on the base serial port /dev/ttyACM0 by default (default_robot.launch.py:35-64) and can start a joystick teleop (bringup.launch.py:29-30, 101-105), and the documentation says Gazebo preserves the microcontroller's interface (docs/base_controller.md:85-87); the same /cmd_vel publication would move a real base if the endpoint is a hardware graph, where no world exists and the e-stop fails closed

operator_required.reason: the clone states no numeric bound for geometry_msgs/Twist.angular.z on /cmd_vel; the joystick scale and the Nav2 velocity smoother are client/navigation settings, not the drive plugins' accepted range, and the operator supplies the signed yaw-rate envelope

operator_required.name: publish_cmd_vel
operator_required.reason: the clone states no numeric bound for geometry_msgs/Twist.linear.x on /cmd_vel; the joystick scale and the Nav2 velocity smoother are client/navigation settings, not the drive plugins' accepted range, and the operator supplies the signed forward/reverse envelope

safe_state.description: The world turtlebot3_world is paused: after the WorldControl pause two fresh stats samples, 40 ms or more apart within 600 ms, reported paused true, so the world does not step and the drive plugins apply no velocity; it is the paused flag in that window, not a measured standstill, it needs the operator-run ros_gz bridges, and the GUI, a WorldControl client or a step request can unpause or step the world.
